title: Learning to Rotate: Quaternion Transformer for Complicated Periodical Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Time series forecasting is important and challenging, including forecasting with complicated periodical patterns and long sequences.

gap.claim: Few existing models handle multiple periods, variable periods, and phase shifts, while dot-product attention has quadratic complexity that hampers long-sequence modeling.

contributions.claim: The authors design Quaternion Transformer (Quatformer), whose learning-to-rotate attention uses quaternions to learn period and phase information for intricate periodical patterns.
The framework includes trend normalization for hidden-layer series representations, accounting for the slowly varying characteristic of trend.
The framework decouples learning-to-rotate attention using global memory to achieve linear complexity without losing prediction accuracy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On multiple real-world time series datasets, the authors report an average 8.1% MSE improvement over the best state-of-the-art baseline.
On multiple real-world time series datasets, the authors report up to 18.5% MSE improvement over the best state-of-the-art baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series forecasting is a critical and challenging real-world problem.
Transformer-based forecasting models address long-range dependencies, and some models use series decomposition to expose temporal dependencies.
Existing models have limited ability to handle complicated periods and face quadratic attention complexity for long sequences.
Quatformer addresses these challenges with learning-to-rotate attention, trend normalization, and globally memory-based decoupling.
The authors report MSE improvements on multiple real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework explicitly models period and phase information with quaternion-based learning-to-rotate attention.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly representing periodic structure may help when temporal patterns vary in period or phase.

application.claim: For forecasting tasks with multiple or shifting periods, consider architectures that learn periodic and phase representations directly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported real-world datasets or which pattern types benefit most.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset names, forecasting horizons, evaluation protocol, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not provide ablations separating the effects of the three components.
The abstract does not detail how linear complexity is measured or implemented.
